chapter: The union and the 1920s-30s band scene
title: Alma Hightower and her student bands
summary: Howard and Collette recall Alma Hightower as a fine teacher whose band, with Melba Liston and Vi Redd among those who came through, played outdoors at 41st and Central.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: You played with everybody around here, and everybody thought the world and all of you. And Alma
Hightower was the one that you played with that lady, she was tickled to death about you.
Yeah, that would be good to get that down, because a lot of people don't know about Miss Hightower.
And some of the people who came through there, because I know some of them. Can you remember anybody?
Vi Rhett. Now, you know one thing? Those things come right out through my mouth when somebody mentions -- somebody names --
But you remember Melba Liston and Redd and that gang.
Do you remember Arthur? (inaudible) trumpet player?
What was his name? Arthur, Arthur. You don't know his name, do you?
(Inaudible) I forget. It'll come to me, too, like we're doing here.

But, anyway, I didn't really know Miss Hightower very well. What was her background and why was she doing that? Because she had that band playing out of that station every day. They would be out there when it was playing those horns cold, raining and whatever else.
Well, all I knew was that she was a very fine teacher. She was a very fine teacher.
She'd (Inaudible) keep them out there, that that was a way to --
Keep them playing, and she was going around, different places, with -- saying, my band, this and
my band, that. And they were working, all the time.
